question.text: Which of the following statements about portfolio rebalancing is FALSE?

answer.text: Rebalancing helps maintain the portfolio's target risk exposure
Rebalancing enforces a "sell high, buy low" discipline relative to the target allocation
Rebalancing involves transaction and tax costs, which the manager should recognise when choosing rebalancing frequency or tolerance bands

explanation.text: The Logic: Rebalancing is a risk-management discipline. The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook (pp.396-397) supports that rebalancing maintains the target risk exposure and naturally implements a "sell high, buy low" rule relative to the target. Pages 176 and 396 also support that rebalancing carries transaction and tax costs, which the manager weighs when choosing frequency/tolerance bands. Page 140 makes clear that securities investments carry no assurance or guarantee — so the FALSE statement is the one claiming rebalancing guarantees returns. The Trap: The original option C ("Helps tax efficiency (can hurt if purely time-based)") could be read as ALSO false, because the workbook treats taxes as a rebalancing cost rather than as tax efficiency. That ambiguity gave candidates a second defensible "FALSE" answer. Options A and B remain clearly true under pp.396-397. Note: The original item was a double-answer trap because option C could be argued as false under pp.176 and 396. Option C has been rewritten to state the source-supported view (rebalancing involves transaction and tax costs that the manager should recognise), making it unambiguously TRUE. The "guarantees returns" statement remains the unique false answer.
